correctness.rationale: For connected complete multipartite graph with r>=2 positive parts, N total, s=min n_i and k>=2, the formula gamma_krt=min{N,2k,k if s<=floor(k/2) else s+floor(k/2)+1} has explicit constructions. Lower bound: W<N forces an empty vertex; W<2k forces a fully labeled part A (otherwise each color must occur in two other parts relative to some empty). With a=|A| and p singleton vertices, support requirements imply W>=k+p and W>=2a-p+1. For a>floor(k/2) their integer minimax gives a+floor(k/2)+1, while the small-part case needs at least k incidences. This covers all boundary cases, including k odd. Fresh independent definition-level exhaustive checks over several profiles through order 6 for k=2,3 agree; source supplied larger checks were not accepted as proof.

value.rationale: An exact formula for a recognized computationally difficult domination invariant over the entire natural class of complete multipartite graphs, all k>=2, strictly extends the established biclique slice. The fact that only N and minimum part size control the optimum follows from a nontrivial singleton-support structural argument and is useful for generalized-prism total domination; this is more than an arbitrary finite census.
